subject: maths
question:
Rs. 9000 is lent at the annual rate of 20 percent for 2 years. Which of the following is statement(s) is/are correct?

I. Simple interest to be received on this sum is Rs. 3500.

II. Compound Interest (compounding annually) to be received on this sum is Rs. 3960.
solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹9000

Rate (r) = 20% per annum

Time (t) = 2 years

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (S.I.) = P × r × t / 100

Amount (A) = P × (1 + r/100)t

Compound Interest (C.I.) = A - P

**Calculations:**

1) Simple Interest:

S.I. = 9000 × 20 × 2 / 100

⇒ S.I. = 9000 × 40 / 100

⇒ S.I. = 360000 / 100

⇒ S.I. = ₹3600

**Statement I is incorrect: Simple Interest is ₹3600.**

2) Compound Interest:

A = 9000 × (1 + 20/100)²

⇒ A = 9000 × (1.2)²

⇒ A = 9000 × 1.44

⇒ A = ₹12960

C.I. = A - P = 12960 - 9000

⇒ C.I. = ₹3960

**Statement II is correct: Compound Interest is ₹3960.**

**∴ Only Statement II is correct.**
